children: will be announcing earnings results this Monday after market hours. Here’s what to look for.

Cincinnati Financial missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $2.97 billion, up 6.9% year on year. It was a slower quarter for the company, with a significant miss of analysts’ EPS estimates and a slight miss of analysts’ net premiums earned estimates.
Is Cincinnati Financial a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Cincinnati Financial’s revenue to grow 5.2% year on year, slowing from the 12.1% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Cincinnati Financial has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Cincinnati Financial’s peers in the property & casualty insurance segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. RLI delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 5.3%, beating analysts’ expectations by 0.5%, and Travelers reported flat revenue, topping estimates by 0.7%. RLI traded up 2.5% following the results while Travelers’s stock price was unchanged.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the property & casualty insurance segment, with share prices up 5.1% on average over the last month. Cincinnati Financial is up 8% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $188.83 (compared to the current share price of $175.59).
